title: Differentiate between On-Page SEO and Off-Page SEO
summaryPoint: On-Page SEO involves optimizing elements directly on the website, while Off-Page SEO focuses on external authority and incoming signals.
keyPoints: On-Page SEO includes activities carried out directly on web pages, such as optimizing title tags, meta descriptions, image ALT text, heading tags (H1-H6), and clean page URLs.
Off-Page SEO includes activities carried out outside website boundaries, such as acquiring high-quality backlinks, social media marketing, and directory submissions.
On-Page SEO improves content indexing and readability, while Off-Page SEO increases search engine domain trust and page ranking.

title: Differentiate between White Hat SEO and Black Hat SEO
summaryPoint: White Hat SEO adheres strictly to search engine policies, whereas Black Hat SEO attempts manipulation and risks search engine penalties.
keyPoints: White Hat SEO strictly conforms to search engine guidelines, focuses on relevant human audience content, and builds sustainable long-term rankings.
Black Hat SEO uses deceptive techniques such as keyword stuffing, doorway pages, and hidden text/links to deceive search crawler bots.
Engaging in Black Hat practices leads to search penalty de-indexing or permanent domain bans from search results.

title: Explain Page Rank and Search Engine Spiders
summaryPoint: Spiders discover and catalog web content, whereas PageRank calculates the relative importance and authority of indexed pages.
keyPoints: Search Engine Spiders (also called web crawlers or bots) automatically browse websites by following links across the internet to discover, fetch, and catalog page content.
PageRank is an algorithm developed by Google that evaluates incoming hyperlink quality and quantity to determine a page's authority score.
Pages linked from high-authority domains pass link equity, directly improving their search result placement.

title: Explain the Importance of Meta Tags in Search Optimization
summaryPoint: Head metadata elements supplying essential machine-readable summaries directly to search engine crawlers.
keyPoints: <meta name="description"> provides a concise snippet of webpage contents displayed below the link on search engine result pages (SERPs).
<meta name="keywords"> contains relevant search keywords associated with the page topic.
<meta name="robots"> instructs web spiders whether to crawl and index the page (index, noindex) and follow its links (follow, nofollow).
